q: My baby is 16 weeks old, and I feel like I’m fighting him to sleep every single time I try to put him down. Naps, bedtime—it doesn’t matter.
cx: Parent of a 16-week-old getting three to four hours of sleep a night.

q: My husband works a physically demanding job to support our family, so I try not to rely on him overnight because he really needs his rest. But that also means I’m carrying most of this alone at night
cx: Same parent on why she covers the nights.

q: today I tried my moms advice of just going about my day to see if he will sleep whenever he wants. We ended up 5 1/2 hours later with no nap
cx: Same parent on following her own mother's advice.

q: When I first had him I thought, “I’m not going to time anything, and just let him sleep when he wants!!” Oh I was so naive. 🥲
cx: Same parent, now planning the 3/3/3 method.

q: We have tried everything, cry-it-out, chair method, every method in the book. (and all other tips, white noise, dark room, same routine)
cx: Father of an almost-10-month-old who never sleeps more than 30–40 minutes.

q: We have seen a pediatrician who just shrugged their shoulders and said HTFU..
cx: Same father.

q: The constant fear of her waking up screaming prevents me from fully relaxing, it's like sleeping with one eye open always prepared to try and calm her down.
cx: Same father, who now does most of the active night effort.

q: Anyone got any encouraging words or success stories to share? I just need to hear that there is a better future on the other side...
cx: Same father.

q: the overhype in sleep training seems to contain a lot of success bias... if it's not working , it's the parents fault for "not sticking to it"
cx: Same father agreeing with a commenter that some babies just don't respond.

q: 10 hours pod cast about ww1 seems to work the best but far from every time
cx: Same father on sound tracks they've tried.

q: I had a work trip I could not miss but was allowed to bring on my husband for support (the trip was long and I was breastfeeding) and ever since we got back about a month ago everything has gone out the window.
cx: First-time mother of an 8-month-old whose improved sleep collapsed after travel.

q: I’m looking into the 3/3/3 bc I can’t really imagine letting her cry for more than 3mins. Also willing to do Ferber method but capping the crying at 3mins each time - not sure if that’s at all counterintuitive?
cx: Same mother, never trained before.

q: we sleep trained her for bedtime using Fuss It Out (FIO). Took her 11 nights to fall asleep independently at bedtime.
cx: Parent of a 5.5-month-old, three weeks after starting FIO.

q: Past two nights we’ve extended the wake window just by 5 mins and it’s definitely helped.
cx: Same parent two days after a commenter's detailed reply.

q: Babe got sick so we had to recalibrate a little. We never got to the 2.75 last wake window before she got sick.
cx: Same parent ten days later: illness interrupted the fix.

q: Feeling a bit lost again
cx: Same parent after the wake windows shifted following illness.

q: We are traveling in May and I know her schedule will get very thrown off by this.
cx: Same parent, planning to revisit training after the trip.

q: I started actually with the first wake window and extended it to 2.5 which ended up sorting out the nap refusal for nap 2 which was creating a wonky long second wake window. Wake windows are now 2.5/2.5/2.5/2.5 and bedtime has been so much smoother
cx: Same parent, sixteen days after posting, crediting one commenter.

q: I want to thank you so much for taking so much time to write such thoughtful and helpful advice.
cx: Same parent to the commenter who coached them across three weeks.

q: I'm now back at work and I really can't do this anymore. I love her to bits, but I just can't function on such small chunks of sleep.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 12-month-old who has rarely slept six hours.

q: if she can't calm/regulate with our support during those moments, how on earth could we try to make her do it herself?
cx: Same mother on why they won't try any form of CIO.

q: I told the health visitor how bad her sleep is and they basically said that whilst it's on the bad end, until 18-24 months that's still considered normal and they can't help until then.
cx: Same mother at the 12-month developmental review.

q: I constantly see things online about babies barely out of the newborn phase sleeping 8-10 hours and I just want to cry. When does it get better?!
cx: Same mother.

q: My husband and I do take turns getting her back to sleep in the night, but I'm a very light sleeper so even when he gets up to resettle her I still wake up
cx: Same mother.

q: I had read stories of happy tear-free bedtimes after 3-4 nights. Our other 13 nights have looked like: 23 min crying, 12, 22, 10, 6, 14, 9, 12, 11, 7, 14, 11 and one EUPHORIC 13th night where he didn't cry at all.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 6.5-month-old on night 14 of Ferber.

q: I hate that he cries through most of the bedtime routine, which is supposed to be a cozy time to wind down. He must have a negative association with the whole process.
cx: Same mother.

q: it kills me that we are putting him through all this crying and it isn't getting better after two weeks.
cx: Same mother, daycare two weeks away.

q: My return to work was fast approaching and the sleep deprivation was getting insane so we turned to Ferber.
cx: Same mother on why they started.

q: We tried this right away and he fell asleep in 5 min with minor grumbling 🙌 He got up once at 2:15 to eat BUT woke up chirping for the day at 5:40.
cx: Same mother the next night after a commenter's change.

q: I’m feeling house trapped. I wish desperately I could go out but if I don’t let my baby nap then we have a horrible night and I’m sleep deprived and miserable.
cx: Mother of a 7-week-old who only naps in a carrier.

q: I follow wake windows and use eat play sleep as a guide. I just can’t get timings down.
cx: Same mother.

q: LO is almost 6 months old and seems to have 180d on his sleep habits. He was sleep trained at 4.5 months
cx: Parent whose trained baby started fighting the crib for naps a week ago.

q: he struggles with the 2nd nap irrespective of wake window - I have tried 2.5, 3, 3.5.
cx: Same parent.

q: I wish they could reliably tell us!
cx: Same parent on guessing the baby's needs.

q: her dad works 14hr days so thats no help, my mom works and lives an hr away so I cant even drive in peace
cx: Parent of an 8-month-old who wakes at 4am and wants to be held all day.

q: im exhausted Im even thinking of going to work so I can get some time away.
cx: Same parent.

q: ive tried letting her cry it out but she literally doesnt stop crying.
cx: Same parent.

q: im losing my mind. I have to basically hold this kid 24/7.
cx: Stay-at-home father of a 10-week-old who has tried a long list of bassinet changes.

q: There is no me time, no wife and I time, can't clean.
cx: Same father.

q: Unfortunately with my wife's work schedule and our 4 year old (he slept wonderfully) I am the primary care giver. She gets home and has 4 hours before she has to be in bed (she wakes up to pump)
cx: Same father on why he covers everything.

q: we’re re starting sleep training and I was wondering wha everyone considers “crying too hard”?
cx: Pregnant mother of a 17-month-old trained at 9 months who now fights sleep.

q: She definitely cries harder now than when she was 9 months and can talk and stuff so it’s a lot of screaming and “mama” “dada”.
cx: Same mother on retraining a toddler versus a baby.

q: I feel like her sleep went back to being good for a week or 2, then she popped 2 teeth, was sick on an off and learning to babble, sit up, etc. and since then I feel like sleep is a mess.
cx: Parent of an 8-month-old after the 6-month regression.

q: She used to sleep 7-7…. I’m sure I am doing something wrong since we have never sleep trained
cx: Same parent.

q: I will say there's no way I'm doing cry-it-out, so how can I get him to sleep independently without traumatizing him?
cx: Parent of a 6-month-old who wakes within an hour in the crib.

q: my husband is currently in school and so I've been taking nights solo (only 8 weeks left!). I can't lean on him at the moment to get some sleep, but I desperately need it.
cx: Same parent.

q: We’ve been at this for a while and it’s starting to drive me a bit crazy, feeling like I’ll never have an evening to myself, with my partner, be able to get our parents here to babysit and so on!
cx: Nursing mother of a 10-month-old who naps well but wakes screaming when put in the crib at night.

q: My partner is helpful but not bringing much to the table in terms of ideas or initiative. He of course says he will support whatever I want to do, but this still leaves the decision and planning up to me
cx: Same mother.

q: I’ve tried tried moving my 5 month old to baby food to get increased calories and fuller to her her sleep. It worked 2 nights and it’s back to the same old .
cx: Parent of a 5-month-old and a sick 5-year-old.

q: My partner works 6-7 am until sometimes 6 pm. I’m alone all day with the baby that doesn’t nap for long. I’m with her all night
cx: Same parent.

q: She was sleeping fund and 12 hr nights until 2 weeks ago and now I’m struggling.
cx: Same parent.
